Placeholders (lib/case-adapt.ts): {A} {onA} {B} {onB} {sells} {where} {onSells} {places} {count} {system} {System} {inStock} {andSystem} {everywhere} {item} {items} {Item} {Items} {variant} {variants} {Variants}. seo.title: Case study: sneaker reseller stock in sync across StockX and Alias · Coelor
seo.description: How a Dutch sneaker reseller keeps StockX and Alias in sync with its warehouse: sold-out sizes switched off every 10 minutes, marketplace sales off the warehouse stock within minutes, 31,000+ sizes checked.

real.gap: A size sold on StockX stayed live on Alias and the other accounts until someone paused it by hand.
real.fix: Sold-out sizes are switched off on every account every 10 minutes, and every sale comes off the Picqer stock.

hero.sub: How a Dutch sneaker reseller stopped pausing sold-out sizes by hand and stopped typing marketplace sales into its warehouse system.

hook.headline: Selling {where} usually means this.
hook.body: Every card below is work someone on your team does by hand today. Each one is a job the sync takes over.
hook.footer: Recognise two or more? That is exactly the work we automate.

items.title: Shop counter and web out of step
items.body: Something sold at the counter stays for sale {onA} until someone takes it off by hand.

items.title: The one-off piece sold twice
items.body: Each piece exists once. When it sells {onB}, it is still for sale {onA} until someone remembers to take it off.

items.title: Buy-ins listed by hand
items.body: Every {item} you buy in or take in trade is counted, photographed and then listed {onSells}, one by one.

items.title: Several shops, one stock
items.body: Each location keeps its own count, so nobody knows what is really free to sell {onA}.

items.title: Every product built twice
items.body: A new {item} goes live {onA}, then someone builds the same listing again {onB}: title, photos, {variants} and price.

items.title: The last one sold twice
items.body: The last {variant} sells {onA} while it is still live {onB}. One buyer gets a cancellation, and the platform counts it against you.

items.title: Stock fixed by hand after every sale
items.body: Something sells {onB}, and someone lowers the count {onA}{andSystem} before the next buyer comes.

items.title: One product, managed in {count} places
items.body: A new price, a better photo or a fixed title is typed into {places}, one by one.

items.title: Orders typed into {system}
items.body: Orders {onA} are copied into {system} by hand, so the stock and the picking list are right.

items.title: The real count lives in a spreadsheet
items.body: The only complete stock list is a sheet someone keeps up to date, and {A} is always a little behind it.

items.title: Listings paused one by one
items.body: After each sale someone pauses the same {variant} on every other platform, one account at a time.

items.title: {Variants} spelled ten ways
items.body: The same {variant} is written one way in {system} and another on each platform, so nothing matches without a person.

items.title: New stock entered by hand
items.body: A delivery arrives, and the new count has to go into {places} before it can sell.

items.title: Returns put back by hand
items.body: A returned {item} is checked, then added back to the stock by hand, {everywhere}.

setup.headline: The warehouse is the single source of truth.
setup.body: Coelor sits between the marketplaces and the warehouse. It reads stock from the warehouse, switches off sold-out sizes on every marketplace account and brings every sale back.
before: Sold-out sizes paused by hand after each sale
Marketplace sales typed into the warehouse system
A size could sell twice before anyone noticed
after: EU and US sizes read from 31,000+ product names and linked
Sold-out sizes switched off on every account every 10 minutes
StockX and Alias sales off the warehouse stock within minutes
Every automatic delisting posted to the team chat

steps.title: Read and link every size
steps.body: EU and US sizes are read from each product name, more than 31,000 of them, and linked to the same size on StockX and Alias. Exceptions can be linked by hand.

steps.title: Switch off sold-out sizes
steps.body: Every 10 minutes the whole warehouse catalogue is checked, and any size with no free stock is switched off on every marketplace account.

steps.title: Bring every sale back
steps.body: StockX sales are picked up every 5 minutes and Alias sales every 7. Each one comes off the warehouse stock with its order number.

steps.title: Report and test every action
steps.body: Every automatic switch-off is posted to the team chat, and every change can run in test mode first.

offer.headline: From first call to live sync, in test mode first.

items.title: A 30-minute call
items.body: We map your platforms, your stock flow and where the hand work is.

items.title: A written scope
items.body: What gets connected, what runs when, and a fixed quote.

items.title: Live in 3 to 6 weeks
items.body: Every change runs in test mode next to your team before it goes live.

items.q: Do we have to change our webshop or stock system?
items.a: No. Coelor connects to the systems you already run through their APIs. If a system has no API, we work from its exports.

The ones you already use: webshops, marketplaces, tills and warehouse systems, through their APIs, or from their exports where there is no API. The first build connected StockX and Alias to Picqer and Google Sheets.

items.q: What happens if a platform's API goes down?
items.a: Runs back off and retry when a platform is slow or rate-limits. A sale is only marked as handled after it has come off the stock, so a failed run is picked up again on the next one.

items.q: Can we see what it will do before it changes anything?
items.a: Yes. Every change can run in test mode first, which logs what it would do without doing it.
Most builds take 3 to 6 weeks from the first call, including the dry-run period next to your team.
